properties.decision:
How req:a-design-states-how-premises-support-a-conclusion-and-reflow2-checks-it-follows is shaped.

CHOSEN (Anthony, 2026-10-14):
- WHERE THE RULE LIVES: "A step record". A new record type sits between the premises and the conclusion: his picture's Operation box. It holds the rule (all, any one, k of n, or a named rule such as modus ponens), the warrant, and later who confirmed it (req:a-design-can-be-a-proof). Premises link in and the conclusion links out. A conclusion with no inference reads exactly as it does today.
- ITS NAME: "Inference". Its "also called" list (req:the-vocabulary-is-served-in-a-fields-own-terms) would carry operation, proof step, gate (fault trees) and strategy (assurance cases).

CONSIDERED AND NOT CHOSEN:
- A SETTING ON THE CONCLUSION. It is smaller, but it cannot name a rule or record who confirmed a step, so proofs would have needed the record later anyway.
- A SETTING ON EACH LINK. OR and k-of-n belong to the group of premises, not to any one link.
- THE NAME "Operation", his picture's word. It is easily confused with "operations" (a system in service) and with a software operation, both of which reflow2 already uses.
- THE NAME "Deduction". Too narrow: "any one of two sensors" is redundancy, not a deduction.

WHY IT WAS ASKED FIRST: whatever is added to the served vocabulary can only be removed through a release that announces it (the 2026-10-13 amendment to req:the-mcp-server-keeps-working-as-is-and-door-improvements-are-additive-or-opt-in). So the shape was settled before any code.
properties.name: An inference is its own record, named Inference, between its premises and its conclusion, and holds the rule by which they support it
properties.rationale: Asked as two multiple-choice questions on 2026-10-14, after his "go" on building C. He picked the recommended option on both. Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_019Xbw6PG9mXJiU2Sb421fnq
